title: SLA-lane intake and automated shadow trials for experimental vs certified model variants
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers request different guarantees for model variants (stability, latency, regressions). Our current intake is one-size-fits-all which slows enterprise adoption and creates friction for experimental model submissions. Goal: Create SLA-driven intake lanes that separate 'experimental' submissions from 'certified' catalog entries and implement an automated shadow-trial pipeline to collect real traffic signals and safety/eval metrics before certifying and/or pinning a variant. Scope: intake rubric, scoring, canary->certified pipeline, automated shadow job infra, pin/sunset automation, dashboarding for decisioning. Out of scope: billing changes and Dedicated infra procurement (handled by a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: New intake form exposes SLA lane selection + auto-surface of enterprise affinity score
Automated shadow-job can be scheduled for a submitted variant and mirrors configurable percent of production traffic for a minimum of 72 hours
Shadow run gathers latency, token-cost delta, top-5 failure modes, and can compute eval-gate pass/fail based on configurable thresholds
Clear canary->certified promotion path exists with manual approval gates for any high-risk enterprise requests
Pin/sunset automation applies a configurable stability buffer (e.g., 14 days of stable shadow metrics) before automatic pinning and a 30-day usage-based sunset window if deprecation is triggered
Console includes per-variant dashboard tiles for shadow metrics and a one-click 'promote to certified' action that records audit log and starts rollout
steps: Define intake SLA lanes (experimental / standard / enterprise-certified) and scoring criteria with PM and Sales
Implement intake form changes and backfill existing catalog items with lane metadata
Build shadow-run scheduler in orchestration layer with traffic mirror hook and result collection endpoints
Add eval gating module to compute pass/fail and produce a standardized report used by the cert board
Create console dashboard views for shadow runs and an approval workflow that ties to audit logs and release history
Implement pin/sunset automation with safe-rollback policies and notification hooks for customers/stakeholders
Pilot with 3 customer-requested variants (mix of open-source and partner models) and iterate on thresholds
decisions: Use shadow-mirroring (non-blocking) vs progressive traffic serving for initial signal collection to avoid customer impact
Require 72 hours minimum of shadow traffic to avoid noisy short-run signals; adjust by model class if necessary
Promote to certified only after eval gates pass AND product/ricert board sign-off for enterprise lanes
Automatic pinning will be opt-in for customer-requested enterprise certifications to respect contractual obligations
Security review is required for enterprise-certified lane because of audit/logging and KMS interactions

notes: Pilot will prioritize low-risk customers and open-source models to accelerate learning. Track cost delta closely; if cost overhead >7% on shadow traffic, reduce mirror percent and extend collection window. Ensure audit logs record who promoted variants. Follow-up items: billing integration for enterprise lanes, Dedicated capacity reservation hook for certified promotions.
